---
title: Navigation
---

## Overview

HTML pages rendered with Quarto can include a table of contents that
tracks the section structure of the document and lets readers jump to
any section. This page covers the table of contents options; for
site-level navigation (navbars, sidebars, breadcrumbs), see the
[websites guides](../projects/create.qmd).

## Table of Contents

Enable the table of contents with the `toc` option:

``` yaml
---
title: My Document
toc: true
---
```

By default the table of contents shows headings up to level 3 and
renders in the right margin of the page. You can control both:

``` yaml
---
title: My Document
toc: true
toc-depth: 4
toc-title: Contents
---
```

- `toc-depth` sets the deepest heading level included (default: 3).
- `toc-title` sets the heading shown above the table of contents
  (default: "Table of contents", localized to the document language).

## Location

Use `toc-location` to choose where the table of contents appears:

``` yaml
---
title: My Document
toc: true
toc-location: left
---
```

The available locations:

| Value   | Placement                                             |
|---------|-------------------------------------------------------|
| `right` | In the right margin (the default)                     |
| `left`  | In a sidebar to the left of the document body         |
| `body`  | In the document body, above the content               |

On pages of a website project, `toc-location: left` places the table
of contents inside the site's navigation sidebar — after the
navigation entries when the page has a sidebar, or on its own when it
does not.

On narrow screens the left and right table-of-contents sidebars are
hidden; use `toc-location: body` if the table of contents should
remain visible at every screen size.

::: callout-note
The `left-body` and `right-body` values (which show the table of
contents both in a sidebar and in the body) are not supported yet;
they currently fall back to `left` and `right` respectively, with a
warning.
:::
